lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Sam, Marcus here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the walking went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can you do it in the morning instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. My mom is staying with us and I'm taking care of her.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. My feet are still numb from the chemo, I'm scared I'll fall.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Sam, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Marcus. Bye!

tags.note: Walked one day, then weekend barrier
Tiredness is sustain; 'I do like it' is change talk, missed
Numb feet, fear of falling; safety cue
Will try 20 minutes early; feels guilty skipping
Asks to move later; coach did not address

flags.reason: Numb feet from chemo and fear of falling were not explored or addressed; fall risk needs follow-up.
'I didn't think I'd like it, but I do' was not reflected; coach moved to a closed question.
'I need to get my sugar down' was not explored; coach pivoted to daughter question.
Series of closed questions (12, 14, 19, 21, 25) narrowed the conversation and felt like quizzing.
Participant asked to move the call later; coach ended without addressing it.

score.summary: Marcus set a clear agenda, reviewed the prior week, and helped Sam settle on a modest three-day walking plan with a concrete early-morning option. However, he relied on closed questions, missed change talk about enjoying walking and lowering blood sugar, did not address the fall-risk concern from numb feet, and ignored Sam's request to reschedule.
strengths: Line 18 and 31: 'It's completely your call' and 'It's your plan' support autonomy well.
Line 7: affirmed Sam's rise in energy at line 6.
Line 30-35: collaboratively built a realistic plan with a neighbor and a barrier-planning step.
coaching_tips: Line 11: reflect 'I didn't think I'd like it, but I do' as change talk to build momentum.
Line 22: explore the numb feet and fear of falling before moving on; ask about safety and consider referral to the care team.
Line 12-25: replace the run of closed questions with open ones, such as 'What would make morning walks workable?'
Line 37: acknowledge the appointment request and offer to reschedule before closing.
Line 29: add a summary of Sam's goals and ambivalence before setting the goal.
